newsitem.title: ITALY: Hard-left mulls tax to boost Italy chance for Euro.
newsitem.headline: Hard-left mulls tax to boost Italy chance for Euro.

text.p: Communist Refoundation would consider supporting introduction of a special new tax to boost Italy's chances of being part of the single European currency, party leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Tuesday.
Refoundation is locked in disagreement with the centre-left government over the 1997 budget, with Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi pushing for cuts in pension and health spending.
Bertinotti told reporters it would be possible to produce a convincing budget without having to touch pensions and health.

He said he would like to see a graded income tax aimed at people on higher incomes and even, if needed, a special tax to limit Italy's budget deficit, which at present falls outside criteria set for countries wishing to join the planned single European currency from the outset in 1999.
The government is due to unveil its budget on Friday.

Ciampi has already announced that the package will cut 32.4 trillion lire off next year's deficit, but several Italian newspapers reported on Tuesday it might have to cut as much as 40.0 trillion lire to reach its 1997 financial goals.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters during a trip to the Netherlands on Tuesday that his ministers would make a "definitive analysis" on Wednesday or Thursday on the final size of the budget package.
He is due to meet leaders from parties that support his government, including Bertinotti, on Wednedsay to discuss the budget.
